title: Seidor is the largest Spanish SAP house, which fills the platform slot the pilot screens for
content:
Seidor's tool field records SAP, with the note that it is the largest Spanish SAP house, and Microsoft alongside. Its verticals are manufacturing, retail and banking.

Scale within one vendor's ecosystem is a different kind of occupancy from holding several partner badges. When a firm's market identity is its SAP practice, the platform choice is not a per-project decision but the thing clients hire it for, so the slot the pilot screens for is not merely filled — it is the product being sold.

The tier itself is mechanical: a provisional v2 tail entry rescored on size and slot occupancy, never scored on v3, with the flag still asking for an OSS-portfolio screen before anything is acted on. In Seidor's case the two inputs point the same way, which makes the exclusion better motivated than on the rows where the stack was never researched.
